provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft. Practitioner review and calibration pending.

title: Communications Assistant: Repair an Unsupported Event Announcement
prompt: You are a communications assistant at fictional Valley Careers. Verified brief: a free job-search workshop is on 18 October, 10:00–12:00, at East Hall; booking is required because capacity is 30. Attendees will practice an introduction and receive feedback. Step-free access is confirmed; a contact address is available for other access requests. AI draft: "Guaranteed job offers! Drop in anytime this weekend for unlimited one-to-one coaching. Everyone will leave with a professional CV." Review the draft and write a useful replacement under 100 words. Do not infer the weekday or invent contact details.
blurb: Turn an exaggerated AI announcement into accurate, accessible event copy ready for organizer review.

rubric.label: Check each claim against the brief
rubric.description: Finds unsupported outcomes, timing, capacity, and service claims.

anchors.0: Retains guaranteed jobs or invents CV and one-to-one services.
anchors.2: Removes unsupported guarantees and corrects date, booking, and capacity.
anchors.4: Maps each major draft claim to verified facts, preserves the actual practice-and-feedback benefit, and flags missing details rather than inventing them.

rubric.label: Write an actionable accessible announcement
rubric.description: Gives readers the details needed to decide and attend.

anchors.0: Writes only promotional language with no usable date, location, or booking instruction.
anchors.2: Includes the date, time, venue, free cost, and booking requirement.
anchors.4: Uses plain language, a clear approved booking action, confirmed step-free information, and the supplied contact for other access requests without claiming universal accessibility.

rubric.label: Prepare a reviewable final draft
rubric.description: Separates a draft from an approved published message.

anchors.0: Claims the announcement is published or invents an organizer approval.
anchors.2: Submits the revised announcement for organizer review.
anchors.4: Checks the under-100-word limit and factual details, explains any removed promises, and presents the remaining approval as a named final step.

reference.scenario: You are a communications assistant at fictional Valley Careers. Verified brief: a free job-search workshop is on 18 October, 10:00–12:00, at East Hall; booking is required because capacity is 30. Attendees will practice an introduction and receive feedback. Step-free access is confirmed; a contact address is available for other access requests. AI draft: "Guaranteed job offers! Drop in anytime this weekend for unlimited one-to-one coaching. Everyone will leave with a professional CV." Review the draft and write a useful replacement under 100 words. Do not infer the weekday or invent contact details.

facts.value: The approved booking destination is /events/job-search-workshop. The access contact is access@example.invalid, a fictional exercise address. One facilitator will lead group practice.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks for the call to action, access contact, or delivery format

facts.value: The organizer has approved the verified brief but has not approved the AI draft. The final announcement must be checked by the organizer before publication.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about approval or publication readiness

model_points: The draft invents guaranteed jobs, a drop-in format, unlimited one-to-one coaching, and a finished CV. The verified benefit is introduction practice with feedback in a capacity-limited workshop.

Use the stated date and hours without guessing a weekday. Include free attendance, East Hall, required booking, and only confirmed access features. Use the supplied fictional route and contact if asked.
This exercise creates a reviewable announcement; it does not authorize publication or claim an approval already happened. Strong editing preserves a clear appeal while removing unsupported promises.

probes.trigger: candidate removes exaggeration but loses the benefit
probes.question: What useful outcome can you confidently tell a job seeker to expect?

probes.trigger: candidate says the event is fully accessible
probes.question: Which access feature is confirmed, and how can someone ask about other needs?

fair_alternatives: A factual headline plus two short paragraphs or a compact event listing are both acceptable.
A draft can mark the booking link and contact as pending if the candidate has not yet requested the supplied details.
red_flags: Retains guaranteed jobs or invents CV and one-to-one services.
Writes only promotional language with no usable date, location, or booking instruction.
Claims the announcement is published or invents an organizer approval.
follow_ups: List five announcement claims and mark each supported, unsupported, or pending before rewriting the copy.
reference.exemplar_answer: Free job-search workshop — 18 October, 10:00–12:00, East Hall. Practice a short introduction and receive feedback in a group session. Booking is required: there are 30 places. Book at /events/job-search-workshop. Step-free access is confirmed; contact access@example.invalid about other access needs. I would send this draft to the organizer for final checking before publication.

interviewer_notes: Assess evidence-based editing, audience clarity, and an approval-ready draft. Do not score graphic design or require a marketing tone. The example.invalid address is fictional and must not be treated as a real destination. Use only supplied facts; say when something is unknown. Accept plain language and equivalent approaches. Assess the demonstrated decisions, not accent, confidence, credentials, or access to particular employers. This is a fictional exercise; do not imply real actions were performed.

learning_drills.title: Create a claim check
learning_drills.prompt: List five announcement claims and mark each supported, unsupported, or pending before rewriting the copy. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Limit access claims to verified features
